module purpose: This file provides neorv32_sys reset and clock helper logic: neorv32_sys_reset clears, delays and qualifies reset outputs from external, watchdog and debug reset inputs, and neorv32_sys_clock latches enable_i, counts while enabled, and emits divided one-cycle clock-enable pulses on clk_en_o.

use-case flows.value: external reset low clears the reset sequencers and forces all reset outputs low in neorv32_sys_reset
delayed external reset release generated by shifting ones through sreg_ext and exporting and_reduce_f(sreg_ext)
delayed system reset release qualified by rstn_wdt_i and rstn_dbg_i
watchdog and debug reset inputs synchronized to xrstn_wdt_o and xrstn_ocd_o
rstn_i low clears the clock-enable generator state in neorv32_sys_clock
clock-enable generation: enable_i activates counting, cnt and cnt2 track count transitions, and clk_en_o emits one-cycle divided pulses

conceptual assets.concept: External reset release state and output -- when the externally reset domain is allowed to leave reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: A 4-bit state register sreg_ext (line 36) is cleared when rstn_ext_i is low (line 45), then shifts in '1' on each rising edge (line 51), and rstn_ext_o is driven from and_reduce_f(sreg_ext) (line 52). Integrity is established because the release output must match that stored release-progress state for downstream consumers; availability is also established because, once rstn_ext_i stays high, the stored sequence advances on clocks until rstn_ext_o is released. The reset input rstn_ext_i is the asynchronous reset input and is excluded from structural reporting.

conceptual assets.concept: System reset release state and output -- when the system reset output may be released after watchdog and debug qualification
conceptual assets.reasoning: sreg_sys is cleared by external reset (line 47), forced back to zero when either rstn_wdt_i or rstn_dbg_i is low (lines 54-55), shifted toward release only when both are high (line 57), and rstn_sys_o is driven from and_reduce_f(sreg_sys) (line 59). Integrity is established because the system-reset release decision must obey those qualifiers exactly for downstream consumers; availability is also established because rstn_sys_o can become high only after external reset is inactive and both qualifiers remain high across the sequencer clocks.

conceptual assets.concept: Synchronized watchdog-reset indication delivered to other logic
conceptual assets.reasoning: xrstn_wdt_o is forced low while rstn_ext_i is low (lines 68-69) and otherwise captures rstn_wdt_i on the rising clock edge (line 72). Integrity is established by the RTL-visible delivery property that downstream logic receives exactly this synchronized watchdog-reset value; availability is also established when external reset is inactive and clock edges occur. rstn_wdt_i is only forwarded unchanged through this synchronizer, so the registered output is the eligible structural reference here.

conceptual assets.concept: Synchronized debug-reset indication delivered to other logic
conceptual assets.reasoning: xrstn_ocd_o is forced low while rstn_ext_i is low (lines 68-70) and otherwise captures rstn_dbg_i on the rising clock edge (line 73). Integrity is established by the RTL-visible delivery property that downstream logic receives exactly this synchronized debug-reset value; availability is also established when external reset is inactive and clock edges occur. rstn_dbg_i is only forwarded unchanged through this synchronizer, so the registered output is the eligible structural reference here.

conceptual assets.concept: Clock-enable generation state and pulse vector -- whether divided-pulse generation is active and which one-cycle enable pulses are emitted
conceptual assets.reasoning: The clock helper stores an activity decision with `en <= or_reduce_f(enable_i);` (line 129), uses that stored decision to increment cnt or clear it (lines 130-133), copies cnt into cnt2 (line 135), and drives clk_en_o from bit transitions `cnt(bit) and (not cnt2(bit))` (lines 140-147). Integrity is established because both the internal generation state and the exported pulse vector must follow these count/edge relations exactly for consumers of clk_en_o; availability is also established because, after reset clears the state (lines 124-127), asserted enable_i causes the stored state to advance and the specified pulse outputs to be produced. The flow graph leaves clk_en_o unreached from an input because these assignments are recorded as GATED_BY-only expressions, but the RTL lines 140-147 directly define the output and are the authority.
